subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
title: Truthfulness
overview: Truthfulness means telling the truth always, whatever the results may be. In this sub-strand you will learn why telling the truth is important, what Proverbs 12:19 teaches about lies, and how Ephesians 4:25 calls Christians to speak the truth to one another.

lessons.title: Why we should tell the truth
objectives: State the importance of telling the truth.
lessons.intro: A learner breaks a window while playing football. The teacher asks who did it. Should the learner speak up, or keep quiet and let someone else be blamed?
lessons.notes:
### What is truthfulness?
Truthfulness is telling the truth always, no matter what the results are. A truthful person says what really happened, does not add or hide facts to deceive others, and keeps promises.

A lie is saying something you know is not true so that others believe it. Lying can also happen when we keep quiet and allow someone else to be blamed, or when we tell only part of the story so as to mislead.

### Why should we tell the truth?
- God commands it. God is truthful, and He wants His children to be truthful too.
- Other people trust us. Parents, teachers and friends believe what a truthful person says.
- It helps us make and keep friends. Friends stay close to someone they can depend on.
- We have peace in our hearts. A person who lies worries about being found out.
- Lies are found out in the end. One lie often needs another lie to cover it, until the truth comes out.
- It protects innocent people. When we tell the truth, others are not punished for what we did.
- It helps problems to be solved. A doctor can treat you well only if you say truthfully how you feel; a teacher can help you only if you say truthfully what you did not understand.

### Back to the broken window
If the learner owns up and says sorry, the teacher knows what happened, nobody else is punished, and the learner keeps a clean heart. The learner may still need to help repair the window, but people will trust him or her more in future.

Telling the truth sometimes needs courage. Christians can pray and ask God for the courage to be honest.

keyWords.meaning: something said to make others believe what is not true
being honest and doing right even when it is hard

activity.title: Why tell the truth?
steps: In groups, say why you should always tell the truth and list your reasons.
Each group reads its list to the class; the class makes one combined list.
Each learner copies the list and underlines the reason he or she thinks is most important.

practice.question: What is truthfulness?
practice.answer: Telling the truth always, no matter what the results are.

practice.question: Give three reasons why we should tell the truth.
practice.answer: Any three: God commands it; people trust us; we keep friends; we have peace; lies are found out; innocent people are not punished.

practice.question: Is keeping quiet while a friend is punished for your mistake a lie? Explain.
practice.answer: Yes. You allow others to believe something untrue, so it deceives them.

summary: Truthfulness is telling the truth always.
Telling the truth pleases God, builds trust and gives peace.
Lies are found out in the end.

lessons.title: Resisting lies: Proverbs 12:19
objectives: Describe situations where people are tempted to lie and how to overcome lies.
lessons.intro: Some people think a small lie will get them out of trouble quickly. The Bible shows that a lie does not last, but the truth does.
lessons.notes:
### Proverbs 12:19
The Good News Bible says:

"A lie has a short life, but truth lives on forever."

This means a lie may seem to help for a short time, but it is soon found out and forgotten. The truth stays true and continues to stand.

### When are people tempted to lie?
- To escape punishment, for example after breaking something or coming home late.
- To get something, such as saying the school asked for money when it did not.
- To look important in front of friends.
- To avoid work, such as saying "I have finished my homework" when you have not.
- Out of fear, when we think the truth will make someone angry.

### What happens when we lie?
- We lose the trust of others. Even when we later tell the truth, people may not believe us.
- We may need more lies to cover the first one.
- Other people may be hurt or punished wrongly.
- We feel guilty and lose our peace.
- Most importantly, lying is sin; it does not please God.

### How to overcome lies
- Stop and think before you speak.
- Remember that God sees everything.
- Own up quickly when you do wrong, and say sorry.
- Ask God in prayer for courage to tell the truth.
- Choose friends who tell the truth.
- If you have lied, go back and correct it. Say, "What I told you was not true. This is what happened."

### Example
Otieno lost the money his mother gave him for bread because he was playing on the way. He is tempted to say that someone stole it. Instead, he tells his mother the truth and says sorry. His mother is disappointed, but she forgives him and knows she can believe him.

keyWords.meaning: to refuse to give in to something
feeling bad inside because you did wrong
to admit that you did something wrong

activity.title: Flash cards and sharing
steps: Write Proverbs 12:19 on a flash card and decorate it.
Recite the verse in pairs until you can say it from memory.
In pairs, each learner shares a time when he or she did not tell the truth and how it ended.
Together, suggest how the lie could have been avoided or corrected.

practice.question: Recite Proverbs 12:19.
practice.answer: A lie has a short life, but truth lives on forever.

practice.question: Give two situations in which learners may be tempted to lie.
practice.answer: Any two: to escape punishment, to get money or things, to look important, to avoid work, out of fear.

practice.question: Name two ways of overcoming lies.
practice.answer: Any two: think before speaking; remember God sees; own up and say sorry; pray for courage; choose truthful friends; correct a lie you told.

summary: Proverbs 12:19: a lie has a short life, but truth lives on forever.
Lying brings loss of trust, more lies and guilt.
We overcome lies by owning up and asking God for courage.

lessons.title: Speaking the truth to one another: Ephesians 4:25
objectives: Read Ephesians 4:25 and explain its message.
Show a desire to always speak the truth.
lessons.intro: In a family or a class, people depend on one another. If one person lies, everyone is affected. Paul wrote to Christians in Ephesus about this.
lessons.notes:
### Ephesians 4:25
The Good News Bible says:

"No more lying, then! Everyone must tell the truth to his fellow believer, because we are all members together in the body of Christ."

Paul wrote this letter to the Christians in Ephesus. He teaches:
- Christians should stop lying completely.
- Every believer should tell the truth to others.
- The reason is that Christians belong together like parts of one body. The eye, hand and foot need to work together honestly. If one part deceives the others, the whole body suffers.

### Living out Ephesians 4:25
- At home: tell parents the truth about where you have been, how you used money, and whether you have done your chores.
- At school: do your own work in examinations, report truthfully what happened in a quarrel, and admit when you have not done homework.
- With friends: keep promises, do not spread false stories about others, and do not pretend.
- In church: be honest in what you say and do.

### Desiring to speak the truth
A truthful person does not tell the truth only when being watched. He or she wants to be truthful because it pleases God. You can grow this desire by:
- praying every day for a truthful heart;
- thinking about the good results of truth: trust, peace and friendship;
- praising others who tell the truth;
- writing poems and songs about truth.

### A short poem
Truth is a light that shines so bright,
It keeps my heart and my conscience right.
A lie will run but soon will fall,
The truth stands tall for one and all.

keyWords.meaning: all Christians, joined together like parts of one body

activity.title: Poem on always telling the truth
steps: Discuss in groups why Christians are compared to members of one body.
Each learner writes a short poem on the importance of always telling the truth.
Volunteers recite their poems to the class.

practice.question: What does Ephesians 4:25 tell Christians to do?
practice.answer: Stop lying and tell the truth to one another.

practice.question: According to Ephesians 4:25, why should believers tell the truth to one another?
practice.answer: Because they are all members together in the body of Christ.

practice.question: Give two ways you can be truthful at school.
practice.answer: Any two: do your own work in exams; report truthfully what happened; admit when you have not done homework; keep promises.

summary: Ephesians 4:25: no more lying; tell the truth to one another.
Christians belong together like one body, so they must be honest with each other.
Pray for a heart that always wants to tell the truth.

quiz.question: What is truthfulness?
options: Telling the truth only when caught
quiz.explanation: Truthfulness is telling the truth always, whatever the results.

quiz.question: Which of these is a benefit of telling the truth?
quiz.explanation: A truthful person is trusted by others.

quiz.question: Give two reasons why you should always tell the truth.
quiz.answer: Any two: God commands it; others trust us; we keep friends; we have peace; innocent people are not punished.
quiz.explanation: Truth pleases God and builds good relationships.

quiz.question: Complete Proverbs 12:19: "A lie has a short life, but ______."
quiz.explanation: The verse says truth lives on forever.

quiz.question: What does Proverbs 12:19 teach about lies?
quiz.answer: Lies do not last; they are soon found out, but the truth stands forever.
quiz.explanation: A lie has a short life.

quiz.question: Amina lied that she had done her homework. What is the best thing for her to do now?
options: Own up to the teacher and say sorry
quiz.explanation: Owning up and saying sorry is the way to overcome a lie.

quiz.question: Which Bible verse says Christians must tell the truth because they are members together in the body of Christ?
Who wrote the letter to the Ephesians?
quiz.explanation: Paul wrote the letter to the Christians in Ephesus.

quiz.question: How can you grow a desire to always tell the truth?
quiz.answer: Any one: pray for a truthful heart; think about the good results of truth; keep truthful friends; write poems or songs about truth.
quiz.explanation: A desire for truth grows through prayer and practice.
